channel.title: Pratik Dhanave — Blog
channel.description: Long-form writing on multi-agent AI, medical AI governance, HIPAA-aware architecture, and cloud-native systems.

item.title: Building an AML Transaction Monitoring Rules Engine
item.description: Teaches how to build AML transaction monitoring: typology rules (structuring, rapid movement, layering), sliding-window aggregation, alert scoring and deduplication, and case management feeding STR/SAR filing.

item.title: Implementing the FATF Travel Rule Between VASPs
item.description: Teaches how to implement the FATF Travel Rule between VASPs: originator/beneficiary PII exchange protocols (IVMS101, TRP/OpenVASP), counterparty VASP discovery, and pre-transfer verification before on-chain send.

item.title: Resolving Ultimate Beneficial Ownership as a Graph Problem
item.description: Teaches how to compute ultimate beneficial ownership: modeling ownership as a graph, percentage-through-chain calculation, control vs ownership thresholds, and cycle handling to surface >25% beneficial owners.

item.title: Delinquency as a State Machine: DPD Buckets, SMA, and NPA Classification
item.description: Teaches how to model delinquency as a state machine: days-past-due bucket transitions, SMA/NPA classification rules, provisioning triggers, and cure/roll-forward/roll-back logic driven by repayment events.

item.title: Building a Credit Decisioning Engine
item.description: Teaches how to build a decisioning engine: feature assembly from bureau/bank/alt data, scorecard vs ML model serving, policy rules and cutoffs, and adverse-action reason-code generation with an audit trail.

item.title: Building a Sanctions Screening Engine That Controls False Positives
item.description: Teaches how to build sanctions/watchlist screening: list ingestion (OFAC/UN/EU), transliteration and fuzzy name matching, scoring thresholds, whitelisting, and rescreening on list deltas to control false positives.

item.title: Building a Dunning and Retry Engine for Failed Payments
item.description: Teaches how to build a smart retry/dunning system: decline-code classification (hard vs soft), backoff and retry-window scheduling, retry-budget limits, and network-token refresh to recover subscription revenue.

item.title: Building a Deterministic Amortization Schedule Engine
item.description: Teaches how to compute loan amortization deterministically: EMI/annuity vs reducing-balance formulas, day-count conventions, principal/interest split per installment, and prepayment/rescheduling recalculation.

item.title: Building a Daily Interest Accrual Engine
item.description: Teaches how to build a daily interest accrual engine: accrual basis and compounding, accrued-but-unbilled tracking, rate changes mid-period, and idempotent daily accrual jobs that post to the ledger.

item.title: Building Marketplace Split Payments and Connected Payouts
item.description: Teaches how to architect marketplace money movement: platform vs connected-account balances, fee/commission splits, delayed payouts, negative-balance handling, and merchant-of-record vs facilitator models.

item.title: Building a Revenue Recognition Engine
item.description: Teaches how to build a rev-rec engine: performance obligations, deferred-vs-recognized schedules, ratable recognition over time, and how billing events differ from recognition events in the ledger.

item.title: Engineering Escrow: Conditional Hold and Release with Double-Entry Safety
item.description: Teaches how to build escrow and conditional hold/release: segregated escrow ledger accounts, release conditions/approvals, partial releases, and expiry auto-refund with double-entry safety.

item.title: Chart of Accounts and Sub-Ledger Modeling
item.description: Teaches how to design a chart of accounts and sub-ledger-to-GL posting model: account hierarchy, dimensions/segments, contra accounts, and how product events map to balanced journal entries.

item.title: Multi-Currency Accounting and FX Revaluation
item.description: Teaches how to keep books in multiple currencies with a functional/reporting currency: transaction-date vs settlement-date rates, unrealized/realized FX gain-loss postings, and period-end revaluation runs.

item.title: Automating the Financial Close
item.description: Teaches how to automate the financial close: ledger cutoff/freeze, accrual and reversing entries, trial-balance assembly, out-of-balance detection, and soft-close vs hard-close controls.

item.title: RTGS vs Deferred Net Settlement
item.description: Teaches the engineering tradeoffs between gross real-time settlement and deferred net settlement: liquidity vs finality, queue/gridlock resolution in RTGS, and settlement-risk windows in DNS.

item.title: Nostro/Vostro Reconciliation, From the Ledger Up
item.description: Teaches how to reconcile correspondent-bank nostro/vostro balances: mirror-account bookkeeping, expected-vs-actual statement (camt.053) matching, value-date breaks, and unreconciled-item aging.

item.title: Payment-versus-Payment: Settling FX Without Principal Risk
item.description: Teaches how payment-versus-payment settlement eliminates Herstatt (principal) risk in FX: matched trade submission, pay-in schedules, simultaneous conditional settlement, and pay-out with net funding.

item.title: Building a Deterministic Interchange Fee Engine
item.description: Teaches how to build a deterministic fee engine that classifies each transaction into an interchange category (regulated debit, rewards, CPS qualification) and computes interchange + scheme + acquirer markup for merchant statements.

item.title: Designing a Netting Engine That Collapses Gross Obligations Into Minimal Settlement
item.description: Teaches how to build a netting engine that collapses many gross obligations into minimal net settlement positions per counterparty, handling netting cycles, cutoff snapshots, and net-debit-cap enforcement.

item.title: Modeling Card Chargebacks as a State Machine
item.description: Teaches how to model the full card dispute lifecycle as a state machine with reason codes, evidence deadlines, representment, pre-arbitration and arbitration, and provisional-credit ledger entries at each transition.

item.title: Card Authorization, Capture, and Clearing: One Transaction, Three Money States
item.description: Teaches how to model the card transaction as a two-phase (auth then capture) plus clearing/settlement state machine, handling partial captures, incremental auths, auth expiry/reversal, and the auth-vs-settled amount reconciliation.

item.title: Integrating 3-D Secure 2 Without Breaking Your Checkout
item.description: Teaches how to integrate 3-D Secure 2: the 3DS Server, Directory Server and issuer ACS handshake, frictionless vs challenge decisioning, device data collection, and liability-shift outcomes feeding the authorization.

item.title: Network Tokenization and How a Token Vault Shrinks Your PCI-DSS Scope
item.description: Teaches how a token vault and network tokens (TR-31/EMV payment tokens) remove PAN from application systems, cutting PCI-DSS scope, and how token provisioning, cryptograms, and detokenization boundaries are architected.

item.title: Engineering SEPA: Mandates, Sequence Types, and the R-Transaction State Machine
item.description: Teaches how to engineer SEPA SCT and SDD flows: mandate lifecycle storage, pre-notification timing, FIRST/RCUR sequence types, and the R-transaction taxonomy (reject/return/refund/reversal/revocation) as a state machine.

item.title: Threading a UETR Through SWIFT MT-to-MX Migration
item.description: Teaches how to parse legacy MT103/MT202 fields, map them to MX pacs equivalents during coexistence, and thread a gpi UETR end-to-end so a cross-border payment is trackable across correspondent hops.

item.title: Building for Instant Payments: RTP, FedNow, and Request-for-Payment
item.description: Teaches how to build for 24x7 irrevocable instant credit: synchronous ISO 20022 request/response, request-for-payment (RfP) flows, credit-transfer timeouts, and idempotent liquidity checks at the rail with no batch cutoff.

item.title: Modeling ISO 20022 Payment Messages Without Losing Your Mind
item.description: Teaches how to model, validate, and generate ISO 20022 XML payment messages (pain.001 initiation, pacs.008 interbank, camt.053 statements) with schema-driven typing, structured references, and idempotent message identifiers.

item.title: Building a Byte-Level ISO 8583 Codec for Card Authorization
item.description: Teaches how to build a byte-level ISO 8583 encoder/decoder: primary/secondary bitmaps, data-element (DE) field definitions, MTI parsing, and stan/RRN correlation for card authorization messaging.

item.title: Building a NACHA ACH File Processor: Records, Hash Totals, and Return Codes
item.description: Teaches how to build a NACHA file processor: fixed-width file/batch/entry/addenda record hierarchy, hash totals, effective-entry-date windows, and handling R-series return/NOC codes with automated re-presentment logic.

item.title: Controls, Access, and Testing a System That Moves Money
item.description: The last mile isn't code — it's who can do what, who approves it, and how you prove it's correct. Segregation of duties, four-eyes, an auditable change trail, and property tests that assert ledger invariants over thousands of scenarios.

item.title: Reliable Delivery: The Outbox, CDC, and Reconciliation
item.description: You can't atomically update your database and publish a message. The transactional outbox (or CDC) stops you losing events; reconciliation is how you find and classify the breaks when two systems drift anyway.

item.title: Consuming APIs and Handling Webhooks
item.description: Talking to a payment rail is the least reliable part of your system. Treat every outbound call as fallible and reconcile on ambiguity; treat every inbound webhook as hostile — verify, dedupe, ack fast, and go read the truth.

item.title: Idempotency and Full Resumability
item.description: The network times out ambiguously, so every request runs zero, one, or many times. Idempotency keys make many behave like one; full resumability lets a crashed money flow resume from its last committed step.

item.title: Executing Money Flows: Invariants, Reservations, and Overdrafts
item.description: A transfer is a state machine with money on the line. Model the states explicitly, reserve funds before you commit, enforce invariants at every transition, and decide up front what an overdraft even means.

item.title: Audit Trails, Event Sourcing, and the GDPR Problem
item.description: In finance you append, never update or delete. Event sourcing gives a perfect audit trail; the right to be forgotten is where it fights back — and crypto-shredding is how you reconcile the two.

item.title: The Ledger: Double-Entry Bookkeeping
item.description: Every transaction is balanced postings that sum to zero — enforce it at write time. The ledger is append-only, and booking, value, and settlement time are three different clocks you must not conflate.

item.title: Representing Money
item.description: Never store money in a float. Use integer minor units or fixed-scale decimals, round half-even, allocate so splits sum exactly, and treat currency and the FX rate you used as first-class, auditable data.

item.title: Give Every Agent Its Own Credential
item.description: Most teams give a whole multi-agent app one workload identity, so one hijacked agent has every agent's blast radius. Splitting identity across app, cloud, and crypto layers shrinks it to a single role and makes the audit trail provable.

item.title: Human-in-the-Loop: An Approval Gate on Durable State
item.description: Series finale, Lesson 7: a sensitive action pauses for human approval, where suspension is just a Lesson 2 checkpoint marked awaiting_approval, the deadline is checked first so a late yes is void, and the action must be idempotent.

item.title: Policy Is Code, Not a Prompt
item.description: A system prompt saying never delete records is a suggestion the model can be talked out of. A gateway that returns FORBID for the delete tool cannot. Put enforcement where the model can't reach it and prompt injection stops mattering for access control.

item.title: Hierarchical Supervision: Bounded Fan-Out, Ordered Fan-In, Fault Isolation
item.description: Lesson 6: bounded fan-out behind a semaphore, ordered fan-in via a pre-sized results slice, and per-worker fault isolation so one sub-agent panicking becomes one failed result instead of crashing the whole run.

item.title: "maximum recursion depth exceeded": A Durable-Workflow Checkpointing War Story
item.description: Threading an SDK client through a checkpointed workflow crashed with maximum recursion depth exceeded. The checkpoint boundary is a serialization boundary: JSON only, values and keys, and anything non-serializable gets injected out-of-band at the composition root.

item.title: Orchestration and Handoff: Routing Intent to a Specialist
item.description: Lesson 5: a triage router first-matches a keyword to hand intent to a specialist, and the exact point a substring table stops being able to think.

item.title: EXHAUSTED Is Not Failure: Bounding Agent Runs
item.description: The scariest agent failure is the runaway loop that never finishes. Cap every run at max_turns and make EXHAUSTED a first-class outcome, neither a failure nor a silent success, with a typed event stream you can route on.

item.title: Advanced Memory: Threads, Keyword Retrieval, and Lossy Summarization
item.description: Lesson 4: memory is three stores, not one — an append-only thread, a keyword knowledge index, and a lossy first-and-last summarizer — and an honest account of where each local stand-in leaks against Azure.

item.title: Tell the Agent What It's Allowed to Do
item.description: If your gateway will block a tool call, don't make the agent find out by trying, because each blocked attempt is a wasted turn. A capabilities brief aligns what the model thinks it can do with what enforcement actually allows.

item.title: Google ADK Glossary: Every Core Concept in One Place
item.description: The capstone of the series: every core ADK concept defined in one place — agents and orchestration, tools, sessions/state/memory, context and callbacks, runtime and streaming, models, grounding, evaluation, protocols, and deployment.

item.title: Secure Sandboxing: Running Agent-Written Code Behind a Timeout
item.description: Lesson 3: run agent-written code behind a hard timeout with exec.CommandContext, distinguish OK from TimedOut, and face the leak — a subprocess is not a security boundary.

item.title: Governing the Tools You Didn't Write
item.description: An autonomous harness injects its own tools at runtime, tools that don't exist at build time. Fail-closed governance is only complete when it turns that blind spot into a visible block, then allowlists the known-safe internals deliberately.
